correctness.rationale: For each explicit quartic \(q\), the homogeneous polynomial is harmonic, so on \(S^2\), \(\Delta q=-20q\). The support-function curvature tensor is \(I+\varepsilon(\nabla^2q+qI)\), which is positive definite for all sufficiently small nonzero \(\varepsilon\). Bochner and integration by parts give the exact identities \(\int\det A_q=-9\int q^2\) and \(\int q\det A_q=136\int q^3\). Hence surface area and volume depend exactly on the second and third spherical moments. The two displayed quartics have equal second moments \(64/315\) and zero third moments, so their volume, surface area and mean width match. Their fourth moments differ by \(65536/4169165\), forcing different random-width laws because \(w(U)-2=2\varepsilon q(U)\). The packaged exact-arithmetic verifier reproduces the harmonic and moment identities but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result targets a concrete smoothness gap highlighted by the recent primary source. It is not a routine recomputation: the bodies are smooth, strictly convex, centrally symmetric, and have exactly matched volume, surface area and mean width for every sufficiently small nonzero parameter, while a higher scalar width moment certifies different laws. This gives a clean near-spherical test family for future inverse questions and narrows the remaining open simultaneous width-and-brightness strengthening.
